Definition: a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye):--dip.
BiblicalUsage: Bapto means to dip, and it appears in three scenes that could hardly be further apart. Jesus dips the sop and hands it to Judas at the supper, the rich man in torment begs for Lazarus to dip his finger in water and cool his tongue, and the rider on the white horse wears a vesture dipped in blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that one small word ties the supper table, the place of torment, and the day of judgment together. A dipped sop marks the betrayer, a dipped finger is denied to the rich man, and a dipped robe marks the Judge, and I believe none of those dippings is an accident.
